column1: # table and a guest reads the partition table it finds -- ours -- not the one
# it was compiled with. Diverging here is what makes a third-party app fail at
# startup for no visible reason.
# The USB-flashed CardOS lives in `factory` and is never overwritten. Two OTA
# slots alternate for everything else: a CardOS update fetched over WiFi
# selected guest app copied from the card. Either goes into whichever slot is
# not running
column2: so neither can take the running CardOS down. Two slots rather

column1: # than one because you cannot overwrite the partition you are running from
# and the OS has to be able to update itself more than once.
# Two independent ways home
#   1. The guest (or a new CardOS) is marked pending-verify. A guest never
#      confirms itself
column2: so the next reset rolls back to the last CardOS that

column1: #      did. A new CardOS confirms itself once its shell is up; one that
#      crashes first is rolled back the same way.
#   2. Erasing otadata leaves nothing valid to read
#      back to factory. This is tools/back-to-cardos.py
#      hatch when everything else has gone wrong.
# `spiffs` is small because CardOS keeps everything on the card and only
# Arduino guests look for it; they need it to exist and mount
# It was 3.3 MB before the second OTA slot took the space.
# The first three entries sit at their conventional offsets on purpose. The
# Arduino platform flashes boot_app0.bin at a hardcoded 0xe000 and the app at
# 0x10000 regardless of what this file says; CardLaunch found that moving them
# produced a bootloader reset loop
column2: because the app landed in a data partition

column1: # and `factory` stayed empty. CardOS is ESP-IDF rather than Arduino and so is
# not itself subject to that
# their own build expects.
# The data partition is named `spiffs` because that is the label Arduino's
# LittleFS looks for. It holds a LittleFS image regardless of the name. Rename
# it and every Arduino guest that stores anything will fail to mount.
# phy_init sits near the end because the space at the front is spoken for.
